title: Two things that should not happen

cues.text: Here is a farmer. For four years running, his farm has lost money.
Every year, more money went out of the farm than came in. And every year the hole got deeper.
Anybody watching would tell him to stop. He does not stop. He keeps farming.
And here is Nell. Nell owns a small factory, and she has the chance to build a second one.
The sums say the new factory would earn her far more than her money is costing her. On paper, she should build it tomorrow.
She refuses. Not this year. Perhaps not next year either.
Both of them are, in fact, behaving correctly.
And by the end of this film, you will be able to say exactly why — in your own words.
Nell makes the decisions. She owns the factory. Every choice in this film is hers, and she is sensible — not timid.
Marshall carries the textbook. He always gives the standard answer. He is right when the world is calm, and badly wrong when it is not.
And Ava asks the questions you would ask. She never lets Marshall get away with anything.
We start from nothing at all. No economics is assumed. Not one word of it.
a farmer absorbs losses, and will not shut
an owner refuses a project the sums approve
both are correct — that is the film
